description: Any solved result, or a model input (input_capacity, input_demand, availability: no run needed), as one table in one unit (columns, then rows; with 2+ dimensions carriers, components or buses become columns). Name a metric, split it with by, pick scenarios (["solved"] for every solved one; default the open one). year = investment period. E.g. {metric:"capacity", by:["year","carrier"], scenarios:["solved"]}; {metric:"price", by:["time"], time:{every:"month"}} (every:"duration" for a duration curve); one day: {metric:"generation", by:["time","carrier"], time:{from:"2040-07-07"}}. Metrics: capacity, storage_capacity, transmission_capacity, generation, demand, emissions, capital_cost, operating_cost, system_cost, unmet_load, price, state_of_charge, curtailment, capacity_factor, revenue, market_value, capture_rate, lcoe, input_capacity, input_demand, availability. IRP: npv (rate, base_year), levelised_cost (rate, base_year; by carrier to stack it), new_build, retirements, clean_share_of_new_build (by year), share_of_load (carriers); each says its method, and a chart can draw any of them.

by.description: Dimensions to split by. Empty = one total per scenario.

layout.description: wide (default): with 2+ dimensions, carriers (or components, buses) become columns. long: one row per value.

metric.description: One metric name from the list.

scenarios.description: Scenario names or ids, "base", or ["solved"] for every solved scenario. Default: the open scenario.

time.description: With by "time": every = step|hour|day|week|month|year|duration|histogram (default chosen by span); how = sum|mean|min|max. from / to ("2040-07-07", or "2040-07-07T16:00"; a date alone for to means to the end of it) or dates (["2040-07-07"]) narrow it to those days; from alone as a date means that one day. histogram: hours spent in each value bin (time is the bin); bins = a count (default 10) or edges; normalize:"peak" bins each series as % of its own peak; share:true gives % of hours; with by "year", one histogram per year.

bins.description: histogram: a bin count, or the bin edges.

top.description: Keep the N largest carriers/components/buses; the rest become "Other".

name: get_results
